inputs: A local Google OAuth client configuration supplied by environment or an ignored credential file
A current-user refresh grant protected outside Git
An explicit inclusive date range and optional YouTube video id
invariants: The default scopes are youtube.readonly and yt-analytics.readonly; the monetary read scope is opt-in and no write scope exists.
Access tokens remain in memory and refresh tokens are protected locally; neither appears in logs, errors, evidence, or telemetry.
Provider responses and normalized evidence are distinct fields in an append-only caller-supplied Company OS state directory.
Unavailable metrics remain unavailable and are never normalized to zero.
Every API call records endpoint without query, result status, latency, response size, and failure kind without request headers or bodies.
Only explicit per-video evidence can cross into the analytics observation store, with operator-supplied deliverable kind and format.
outputs: ChannelEvidence and VideoEvidence from YouTube Data API v3
AnalyticsEvidence with explicit unavailable metrics from YouTube Analytics API v2
Append-only raw/normalized evidence envelopes and optional MetricObservation records
purpose: Obtains continued read-only access to the company's own YouTube channel, turns Data and Analytics API responses into traceable evidence, and bridges explicit per-video readings into the existing analytics ledger.
risks: Google can revoke a refresh grant or change metric availability; both become explicit authorization or unavailable-evidence outcomes.
YouTube subscriber counts can be hidden or rounded and analytics data can be delayed or revised.
A local OAuth client secret remains the operator's responsibility and must stay outside Git.
title: Read-only YouTube connectivity
